sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Michael Bulkaam. 2021 [Glottolog lists as 2020]. An introduction to Mantsi, a South Bauchi language of Central Nigeria. Draft circulated for comment, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge; printout 1 January 2021. 25 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'Mantsi phonology' (pp.2-5) covers consonants, six vowels with length, tone-bearing nasal prefixes (p.4) and sec. 2.3 Tones (p.5): 'Mantsi has three level tones as well as rising and falling.' Zero occurrences of stress/accent/prominence in the text; ~600-item tone-marked wordlist appended.

sources.citation: Cosper, Ronald. n.d. [uploaded 2021]. Research on Mansi, a West Chadic language, with a comment on Blench and Bulkaam's recent paper. Unpublished paper, Saint Mary's University (Halifax). 13 pp. Academia.edu item 62475787.
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.note: Compares three lexical datasets for Mansi (Shimizu 1978, 107 items; Cosper 1993, 471 items; Blench & Bulkaam 2020) over Shimizu's 107 words to test their validity; finds overall agreement, B&B most divergent. A lexical cross-validation, not a phonology; any remarks on tone transcription are unseen. Low tone relevance -- listed because it is one of only four primary documents on this lect and is not previously listed here.
